title: Adding transaction savepoints interpolated the caller-supplied savepoint name into SAVEPOINT/ROLLBACK TO/RELEASE statements with f-strings.

findings.explanation: A validation function was added that uses an allowlist of safe characters (ASCII letters, digits, hyphens, underscores) to validate savepoint names before they are used in SQL queries. The function rejects any names containing characters outside this set, which prevents SQL injection via savepoint names. This is a strict allowlist approach that effectively neutralizes the SQL injection vector.

The validation function is called before constructing SQL queries with savepoint names in rollback_to(), release(), and savepoint() methods. The validation ensures that only safe characters are present in the savepoint name, preventing SQL injection attacks.

evidence.content:
async def rollback_to(self):
        validate_savepoint_name(self.name)
        await self.transaction.connection.execute(
            f"ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT {self.name}"
        )

    async def release(self):
        validate_savepoint_name(self.name)

findings.explanation: Same mitigation as in postgres.py: validation is performed before SQL query construction for savepoint operations in SQLite implementation.
